name: HPE ProLiant Compute XD series GPU servers (XD685 and siblings)
region: Worldwide; HPE also runs buy.hpe.com as a direct storefront
notes: QUOTE-ONLY, and notably HPE is the one vendor here that routes AI-accelerator buyers to an actual STOREFRONT: Intel's Gaudi page links 'Shop HPE' straight to buy.hpe.com ProLiant compute, so a Gaudi-capable box can be configured and quoted through HPE's own e-commerce rather than a phone call. HPE is also a named partner on AMD's Instinct where-to-buy page. Verified from the XD685 product page: 'The HPE ProLiant Compute XD685 is powered by a choice of NVIDIA or AMD Instinct GPUs, and AMD EPYC 9005 Series CPUs', marketed for large-scale AI model training, NLP and multimodal training; AMD's page describes it as a 6U system with 5th Gen EPYC designed to accelerate large AI model training. The dual-NVIDIA/AMD option is the notable supply fact: it makes HPE a route to a second-source AMD capacity when NVIDIA allocation is the binding constraint. HPE also claims 18 number-one rankings in MLPerf Inference v6.0, which is a performance claim, not a supply datum. No price seen on the page, so null. BASIS as elsewhere: accelerators are configured into the node, not sold as modules. EXPORT CONTROLLED (true). Regime: US BIS advanced-computing export controls (the Oct 2023 interim final rule, 88 FR 73458 - source sup-buy-bis-2023-advanced-computing-controls), which put datacenter accelerators under ECCN 3A090/4A090, added the advanced-computing Foreign Direct Product (FDP) rule, and extended Regional Stability (RS) controls to Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5. For items destined to Macau or Country Group D:5 the rule applies a PRESUMPTION OF DENIAL; other RS destinations get a presumption of approval. Practical effect: which accelerator you can legally be sold, and which SKU counts as compliant, is set by destination and end user - not by the channel.
